notes: Covenant faithfulness that goes beyond what is owed: kindness, loyalty, and mercy bound together. It's what people in a committed relationship do for each other, especially when one can't repay. English has no single word for it, which is why translations vary so much. It's the central word of Ruth.

range.note: Keeping faith with family, friends, or covenant partners.
Doing more than the relationship strictly requires.
Kindness shown to someone in need who has no claim to it.

elsewhere.note: God describes himself as "abounding in loyal love."
The refrain "his loyal love endures forever."
God desires loyal love, not sacrifice.
"To love hesed," part of what God requires.

notes: An old name for God, often in the form El Shaddai, "God Almighty." It's especially common in the stories of Israel's ancestors and in Job. Naomi uses it as she says God has dealt bitterly with her.
uncertain: Where the name comes from is debated. Suggestions include a word for "mountain," a word for "breast" (God as provider), and a verb meaning "to overpower."

range.note: Used as a name or title for God, not a common noun.
Traditionally understood as stressing that God is mighty.

elsewhere.note: God appears to Abram as El Shaddai.
God says he was known to the ancestors as El Shaddai.
One of many uses in Job.

notes: "Naomi" sounds like the word for "pleasant." Back in Bethlehem she asks to be called Mara, "bitter," to match her grief. The idea of bitterness runs through her words in Chapter 1.

range.note: As in bitter water or bitter herbs.
Deep sorrow or a hard lot in life.

elsewhere.note: Marah, the place of bitter water, from the same root.
Hannah prays "in bitterness of soul," the same root.

notes: A close relative with the right and duty to step in for family in trouble: buying back land that had been sold, freeing a relative sold into debt, or keeping a family line alive. In Ruth it starts as a family duty and becomes the shape of the whole story. Elsewhere in the Bible, God is called Israel's redeemer.

range.note: Buying back family land so it stays in the family.
Buying back a relative who sold himself to pay debts.
The relative responsible for justice when a family member was killed.
God acting as Israel's next of kin, rescuing his people.

elsewhere.note: Redeeming land a poor relative has sold.
Redeeming a relative sold into service.
The avenger of blood.
"Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel."
"I know that my redeemer lives."

notes: A broad word covering strength, ability, wealth, and character. It's used of Boaz ("a worthy man," 2:1) and of Ruth ("a worthy woman," 3:11), so the wealthy Israelite landowner and the poor Moabite widow are described with the same word.

range.note: Physical might, often of warriors.
Resources and standing in the community.
A force of fighting men.
Noble, capable character.

elsewhere.note: "A worthy woman, who can find?"
Gideon is greeted as a "mighty man of valor."
David is described as a "man of valor."

notes: Means a bird's wing, and also the edge or corner of a garment. Boaz blesses Ruth for taking refuge under God's wings (2:12); later Ruth asks Boaz to spread his wing over her (3:9). The repeated word suggests Boaz becomes part of God's answer.

range.note: A bird's wing, and so a picture of shelter.

range.sense: Corner or edge of a garment
range.note: The hem or flap of a cloak.
As in "the ends of the earth."

elsewhere.note: "Under his wings you will find refuge."
God spreads his garment over Jerusalem, a picture of marriage.
Tassels on the corners of garments.

notes: A rhyming expression for someone or somewhere left unnamed, like "so-and-so" or "such and such." Boaz surely knew the man's name, but the writer chooses not to give it.
uncertain: Why the writer leaves him unnamed is a matter of interpretation. One common reading: he refused to keep a dead man's name alive, so his own name is left out.

range.note: "So-and-so," "a certain one."
"Such and such a place."

elsewhere.note: David mentions "such and such a place."
The king of Aram plans to camp at "such and such a place."
